kaps_punt: Leesvaardighede: lees met begrip en vlotheid: Lees oor basiese eerstehulp: interpreteer/verduidelik en vertel wat aangeleer is.

items.bewering: Sy het geweet warm tee maak 'n skroeiwond, en dit is ook 'n brandwond.
items.bron: Checked fresh this round; whole lesson checked end to end. Majstro Afrikaans-English dictionary gives 'skroeiwond = scald' (https://www.majstro.com/dictionaries/Afrikaans-English/skroei). NHS 'Burns and scalds' treatment page (https://www.nhs.uk/conditions/burns-and-scalds/treatment/) treats a scald as a burn with the same first aid.

items.bewering: Jy roep 'n grootmens en jy koel die brandwond op dieselfde tyd. Die water wag nie vir die grootmens nie.
items.bron: Checked fresh. NHS: 'Do this as soon as possible'. ANZCOR Guideline 9.1.3 (https://www.anzcor.org/home/first-aid/guideline-9-1-3-first-aid-for-burns): 'the sooner the better'. HSE Ireland, burns and scalds in children (https://www2.hse.ie/babies-children/first-aid/burns-scalds/): 'Cool the burn or scald immediately.' No source says cooling should wait for an adult.

items.bewering: Sy het Sipho op 'n stoel by die wasbak getel en sy arm onder die kraan gehou. Die koel water het oor die rooi plek op sy voorarm geloop.
items.bron: Checked fresh. Western Cape Government Health (https://www.westerncape.gov.za/health-wellness/article/start-safe-protect-our-little-ones-preventable-injuries-burns-season): 'Run cool water over the burn'. NHS: 'Hold the burn or scald under cool running water'. ANZCOR 9.1.3 forbids ice and iced water; the lesson says only 'koel' and never mentions ice.

items.bewering: Die water bly nou twintig minute lank aan (also the title, 'Na twintig minute het Ma die kraan toegedraai', and 'al tien sy vingers twee keer ... Twintig minute')
items.bron: Checked fresh. Western Cape Government Health: 'Run cool water over the burn for 20 minutes'. South African Family Practice 2020, 'Primary management of burn injuries' (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8378189/): cooling shows 'maximum benefit when done for 20 min'. The same figure appears in guidance from the NHS, ANZCOR 9.1.3, the British Red Cross and Health New Zealand. Ten fingers held up twice makes twenty.

items.bewering: Die mou van Sipho se trui was sopnat van die warm tee. Zanele het gesê die nat mou hou die hitte teen sy vel vas.
items.bron: Checked fresh. ANZCOR 9.1.3: remove wet, non-adherent clothing because 'clothing soaked with hot liquids retains heat'.

items.bewering: Ma het versigtig gevoel of die trui aan die vel vassit. Dit het nie vasgesit nie, en saam het hulle die trui stadig uitgetrek.
items.bron: Checked fresh. NHS: 'Remove any clothing or jewellery that's near the affected area – but do not remove anything that is stuck to the affected area.' HSE Ireland: remove clothing near the injury 'unless they are stuck to the skin'. If it is stuck, 'cut around it instead'. Health New Zealand (https://www.healthnz.govt.nz/health-topics/tests-and-treatments/emergencies-and-first-aid/burns): 'Do not try to remove anything that is stuck to the burned skin.' The story checks first and then removes the jersey slowly. That matches all three, and it is the step a child would copy.

items.bewering: Toe het Zanele die kraletjie-armband van sy pols afgehaal. ... Sy het verduidelik dat 'n brandwond kan swel en dat 'n armband dan vassit en druk.
items.bron: Checked fresh. Health New Zealand: 'Remove any jewellery and watches, before the area swells.' St John Ambulance UK, Burns and scalds (https://www.sja.org.uk/first-aid-advice/burns-and-scalds/): remove jewellery 'before the area begins to swell'. ANZCOR 9.1.3: remove 'all rings, watches, jewellery or other constricting items'.

items.bewering: Ma het gesê net die brandwond moet koel word en nie die hele lyf nie. Zanele het 'n droë kombers ... Ma het dit dadelik om sy skouers en sy lyf toegedraai. ... die res van Sipho het warm gebly.
items.bron: Checked fresh. ANZCOR 9.1.3: keep the person warm to reduce the risk of hypothermia, 'particularly small children who may develop hypothermia quickly'. HSE Ireland: keep the child warm with layers and blankets, but 'avoid putting these over the injured area'. The blanket in the story goes round his shoulders and body, not over the arm under the tap. British Red Cross (https://www.redcross.org.uk/first-aid/learn-first-aid/burns): cooling the whole body could cause hypothermia.

items.bewering: Sit gou botter of tandepasta daarop. Ek het gehoor dit trek die brand uit. (Ruben's claim, which the story rejects)
items.bron: Checked fresh. The story is right to reject it. ANZCOR 9.1.3, the NHS ('do not put any creams, oils or butter on burns'), Western Cape Government Health ('Don't apply creams, oils, or home remedies') and SA Family Practice 2020 ('Do not apply any other substance to the burn wound') all say so. The story shows it only as a false belief and corrects it at once.

items.bewering: Maar die koel water haal die hitte uit die vel.
items.bron: Checked fresh. ANZCOR 9.1.3 and the British Red Cross both explain cooling as removing heat from the burn. Cool running water within 3 hours cut the depth of the burn and the need for skin grafts in children: Griffin et al., Annals of Emergency Medicine 2019/20, a study of 2,495 children (https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/31474480/).

items.bewering: Botter hou die hitte in die vel vas.
items.bron: Checked fresh. British Red Cross: 'Butter and cream contain oils. Oils retain heat, which is the opposite of what you're trying to do.' Health New Zealand: do not use oils, 'as they can keep the heat in'.

items.bewering: Tandepasta koel die brandwond nie af nie.
items.bron: Checked fresh. British Red Cross: menthol in toothpaste gives only a surface feeling of cooling and does not help the burn. The NHS-derived wording 'Butter, cream or toothpaste will not cool the area' appears in the search results.

items.bewering: Hulle kan die brandwond ook vuil maak. Ons smeer niks daarop nie.
items.bron: Checked fresh. St John Ambulance UK: creams and gels 'may cause damage and increase the risk of infection'. SA Family Practice 2020: 'Do not apply any other substance to the burn wound.' Western Cape Government Health: home remedies 'can make the burn worse and harder to treat'.

items.bewering: Na tien minute ... 'Die tyd is nog nie om nie. Die water help jou arm nog, al voel jy nou minder pyn.'
items.bron: Checked fresh. ANZCOR 9.1.3 says to cool 'for at least 20 minutes', and Griffin et al. (Annals of Emergency Medicine, 2,495 children) linked the benefit to depth and grafting to 20 minutes, not to how much it hurts. St John Ambulance UK words it 'at least 20 minutes or until the pain feels better'. Its minimum is still 20 minutes, so stopping at ten is too early by every source.

items.bewering: Sy het 'n stuk kleefplastiek los oor die brandwond gelê en niks daaronder gesmeer nie. Sy het die plastiek nie om sy arm gedraai nie.
items.bron: Checked fresh; this is the changed step. NHS: 'When the burn or scald has cooled, lay cling film over it if you can. Do not wrap the cling film around it.' St John Ambulance UK: 'cover the area loosely with cling film, lengthways. Do not wrap the cling film around the burn'. ANZCOR 9.1.3: 'a loose non-stick dressing, preferably clean material e.g. plastic cling film', not wrapped round limbs. The South African source SA Family Practice 2020 says 'Cover the burn wound with cling film or a clean non-adhesive dressing.' The film goes on after the 20 minutes of cooling, which is the order the NHS gives. The Western Cape page prefers 'a clean, wet cloth' but does not rule out cling film, so there is no conflict.

items.bewering: Sy het gesê die plastiek hou die brandwond skoon.
items.bron: Checked fresh. healthdirect Australia (https://www.healthdirect.gov.au/burns-and-scalds) recommends a loose non-stick dressing, with cling film 'a good choice', to prevent infection. The St John Ambulance UK guidance, as summarised in search results, says cling film protects by keeping the area clean. The British Red Cross adds that it 'won't stick to the burn'.

items.bewering: Dit lê los om nie te druk as die brandwond swel nie.
items.bron: Checked fresh. St John Ambulance UK: do not wrap it, 'as the area needs space to swell'. Health New Zealand: 'Make sure the covering is loose, as the burned area may swell.'

items.bewering: Toe het sy besluit om Sipho kliniek toe te neem. ... 'Hy is nog klein, en ek wil hê die suster moet self na sy arm kyk.'
items.bron: Checked fresh. ANZCOR 9.1.3: 'All infants and children with burns should be medically assessed.' British Red Cross: 'If a baby or child has been burned, seek medical advice.' Western Cape Government Health: 'Go to the nearest clinic or hospital', and 'Clinics are often the first point of care' for burns. Taking a four-year-old to the clinic is the South African route.

items.bewering: No superlatives and no analogies in the lesson
items.bron: Read the whole reading piece for superlatives (eerste, grootste, enigste and the like) and for comparisons. There are none. The only false belief in the story, Ruben's 'dit trek die brand uit', is shown as a myth and corrected at once. The other details (Saturday morning, washing on the line, the biscuit tin, the neighbour's dog) are story and cannot be checked.

opsomming: Checked afresh as a whole: every first-aid step and reason a child might copy in the burn story is supported by health-department and first-aid sources, including one South African medical journal. That covers cooling at once without waiting for an adult, a full twenty minutes under cool tap water, taking off the wet jersey only after checking it is not stuck, removing the bracelet before swelling, keeping the rest of him warm, no butter or toothpaste, cling film laid loosely over the burn and not wrapped, and a clinic visit for a small child. The cling-film change settles the earlier uncertainty about a cloth, and nothing needs correcting.
